chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Mansur ibn Yunus, from al-Thumali, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them) who said:

Verily Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, says: 'Indeed among My servants is one who asks Me for something from [the ability to perform] acts of worship so that I may love him, but I turn that away from him so that he would not be pleased with [himself and] his deed.'

key_terms.يَعْجَبَهُ: He is pleased with himself/prides himself

ai.seo_question: Why does God sometimes remove the ease of worship from a servant?
ai.summary: In this profound narration from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the divine strategy of *khud'* (self-admiration) by revealing that God sometimes withholds the ease of worship not as punishment, but as a merciful prevention of spiritual arrogance. This concept, central to Shia asceticism, illustrates how divine concealment (*istirar*) serves to preserve the servant's humility and ensure that worship remains purely for God's sake rather than for self-aggrandizement. It underscores the delicate balance between divine love and the preservation of the servant's spiritual integrity.
